findings.issue: The Surroundings column states temperature changes too absolutely. “Warm” and “Cool” should be “may warm” and “may cool,” or the table should explicitly be limited to a specified calorimetry setup.
findings.evidence: Source 6.1 says that the surroundings “may warm up” when the system releases energy and “may cool” when the system absorbs energy. The draft removes that hedge and makes warming or cooling sound inevitable for every dissolution.

findings.issue: Part (3) equates the peak itself with activation energy. Activation energy is the energy difference from the reactant level to the peak, not the peak or its absolute energy. A correct wording would be: “the reactant-to-peak height is activation energy, a quantity separate from ΔH.”
findings.evidence: Source 6.2 step 3 calls for distinguishing the height to a peak from the reactant-to-product difference, and the draft’s own mechanism table correctly identifies “Reactant level to the peak” as activation energy. Standard chemistry likewise defines activation energy as an energy difference.
